findings.text: The section asserts 'for all 581 ingested content-stage files the per-file HAS_CHUNK count is unchanged (0 files changed) ... no CodeExample or CodeChunk was added or removed'. The only instrument behind it is census.py:60-70, whose query returns sf.chunk_count AS stored_chunk_count; that column is null in all 581 rows of census_before.json, census_after_pass1.json, census_after_pass2.json and census_after.json, and the linked_chunks count the same query returns is 0 for every file in every snapshot. A column that is uniformly null cannot show the property held, and no positive control shows any chunk existed to be counted, so the done-when's 'chunk count unchanged' clause is not demonstrated: either the HAS_CHUNK relationship or direction census.py matches is wrong (an instrument defect) or the files do not carry their text as the plan's premise assumes.

The fragment and the manifest state the pass 'drained (zero unanswered)' and 'pass 7 EXIT=0', but no instrument records either. No line of rejudge_pass1.log through rejudge_pass7.log contains 'unanswered' or 'drain', and no pass log carries an EXIT= sentinel (pass 7's last line is a below-gate path); the only per-pass signal is the summary line 'N ingested file(s) re-judged', which reads 660-740 against a set of 581. The claim may hold, but with no metric for 'unanswered' it is asserted rather than measured.

The paragraph claims 'score_composite IS NULL: 0 files'. census.py measures only the five facet confidences and the status counts; grep for score_composite across the run directory returns it only in the worker's own manifest.md, classification.json and stream.jsonl, never in a census snapshot or a pass log. The count is therefore an assertion about a query that was not saved, and it cannot be reconciled against the evidence the run produced.
